stem: Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?

printed_q: 1. Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?
stem: Which of the following causes jet black appearance of the pupillary aperture?
explanation_verbatim: Pupil is jet-black in the newly born and starts to acquire a greyish tinge as the person gets older due to the continuous addition of new lens fibers throughout life causing light scattering; a process known as senile sclerosis. It is to be noted that in the absence of the lens (surgically removed or posteriorly dislocated), the pupil regains its jet-black color.

stem: A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring. Which of the following might occur as a complication to that patient's condition?

A 22-year-old male patient presented to the ophthalmology clinic with a complaint of seeing bugs or cobwebs together with light flashes. Ophthalmoscopy revealed an evident Weiss ring. Which of the following might occur as a complication to that patient's condition?
explanation_verbatim:
This case is a case of PVD. Complications of PVD may be:
A. Traction at areas of abnormal vitreoretinal adhesions or areas of weak retina may cause retinal tears/detachment
B. Retinal tears/detachment may cause vitreous haemorrhage if a bridging retinal blood vessel is torn.

stem: Which of the following is the best line of management of a diabetic patient presenting with acute angle closure glaucoma together with lower limb edema and dyspnea?
Which of the following is the best line of management of a diabetic patient presenting with acute angle closure glaucoma together with lower limb edema and dyspnea?
explanation_verbatim: Medical treatment of acute angle closure glaucoma (to lower IOP, reduce pain, and clear corneal oedema in preparation for iridotomy). Topical medications: IOP lowering drugs (previously mentioned), miotics & Prednisolone. Systemic medications: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (for IOP lowering) & Osmotic agents: Mannitol (contraindicated in cardiac patients) and glycerine (contraindicated in diabetics).

stem: A 62-year-old diabetic woman with pre-existing proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) is at risk of developing which of the following?
A 62-year-old diabetic woman with pre-existing proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) is at risk of developing which of the following?
explanation_verbatim: Tractional retinal detachment (TrRD) -> Caused by vitreous, epiretinal, or subretinal membrane pulling the neurosensory retina away from the underlying RPE. It is found in conditions such as DR, CRVO, sickle cell disease, ROP, and ocular trauma.

stem: Which of the following is a cause of dilated fixed pupil?

Treatment of amblyopia
Treatment of the cause: spectacles for anisometropia, treat media opacity or ptosis... etc.

stem: Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?

printed_q: 20. Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?
stem: Which of the following is considered a visual field defect that is characteristic of glaucoma?

explanation_verbatim:
Characteristic field changes in glaucoma (particularly primary open angle glaucoma):
A. Paracentral scotomas: multiple isolated scotomata in the zone between 10 and 20 degrees from the fixation point.
B. Arcuate scotoma that arches above and below the fixation point.
C. Nasal step: Due to asymmetric involvement of the arcuate nerve bundles above and below the fixation point.
D. Tubular field (Tunnel vision): The field of vision may constrict until it is limited to a few degrees around fixation.
Fixation (central vision) may be spared until the disease is markedly advanced.
E. End-stage glaucoma: These residual seeing areas may be eventually lost leaving the patient blind.

stem: Which of the following is an adverse effect of local cycloplegics?
Which of the following is an adverse effect of local cycloplegics?
explanation_verbatim:
Systemic toxicity of cycloplegics: (especially in children) causes the following:
1. Increased body temperature
2. Flushing (reddening) of skin
3. Dryness of skin and mouth
4. Irregular rapid pulse
5. Hallucinations, confusion, and delirium
